title: Weak stationarity by eye: does the distribution move?

explain.prompt: The test code applies `subsample_stats` to five series: white noise, a random walk, a trend-stationary series, the TTF price and its log returns. In 4–6 sentences: which ones look weakly stationary and why? Why does the random walk fail even though every shock is pure noise? Can this check tell the trend-stationary series apart from the random walk?
rubric: Weak stationarity = constant mean, constant finite variance and autocovariances that depend only on the lag; white noise and TTF log returns pass the eye test (block means within ≈ 0.15 std, std ratio ≈ 1.1).
A random walk accumulates its shocks: y_t = y_0 + ε_1 + … + ε_t, so every shock is permanent, Var(y_t) = t·σ² grows with time and the block means wander (mean shift ≈ 3.5 std here).
The TTF price behaves like the random walk (block means 17 → 31 €/MWh, std ratio ≈ 4): its level has no fixed anchor.
The trend-stationary series also fails on the means (they climb steadily) but its within-block dispersion is stable (std ratio ≈ 1.0): shocks are transitory around a deterministic line.
The check is a heuristic: it cannot prove stationarity nor separate a deterministic from a stochastic trend — that needs formal tests (ADF / KPSS, next steps) with the right deterministic terms.
